question: How do memos work on Stellar: types, size limit, whether one transaction can carry multiple, which transactions support them, and why do exchanges require them?

golden.answer: A memo is optional transaction-level metadata, at most one per classic transaction: MEMO_TEXT (up to 28 bytes), MEMO_ID (uint64), MEMO_HASH or MEMO_RETURN (32 bytes). Exchanges use it to map deposits into one pooled account to customers. A fee-bump has no outer memo; any memo sits in the inner transaction. An InvokeHostFunction transaction must use MEMO_NONE.
keyFacts: At most one memo per transaction: text (28 bytes), ID (uint64), hash or return (32 bytes).
Exchanges use memos to map pooled-account deposits to customers.
An InvokeHostFunction transaction must use MEMO_NONE; a fee-bump memo is the inner one.
avoid: Do NOT claim multiple memos per transaction or that InvokeHostFunction accepts a memo.

sources.note: validateSorobanMemo: an INVOKE_HOST_FUNCTION transaction with a memo other than MEMO_NONE fails validation.
'The transaction cannot include a memo — the memo must be set to MEMO_NONE.'
CAP-0084 (Protocol 30) adds muxed contract addresses and does not relax the InvokeHostFunction memo rule.
validateSorobanMemo is present in the v30.0.0 tag, gated by protocolVersionStartsFrom(V_25) with no upper bound.

corroboration.claim: Classic transactions carry at most one memo; fee-bump has no second outer memo, and current InvokeHostFunction transactions require MEMO_NONE.
